title: Perdido Street and the Storyville cabarets
summary: He recalls Bunk, Armstrong and Red Happy near Perdido and cabaret bands such as Peter Bocage's at Pete Lala's.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Who was playing around Pedido Street when you were little?

Well, to tell you the truth, the first ones I remember outside of Bunk Johnson when I was small, outside of him was Louis Armstrong when Louis was coming up around his teens. I remember him. I remember him. Red Happy. But I don't know who was on piano. That was playing at the corner of Franklin and Pedido. On a river in downtown corner. He used to have a little honky tonk that. Well, they used to play there every Saturday night. In the meantime, Louie was driving a cold dump car. And I think that was after he got out of Jones' home. Yeah, I think that was after he came out of Jones' home.
What was the name of this town?
I don't know. I never did know the name of it. I never did bump around in them places, you know? So I never did know the name of it.
Did they have many bands in the district when you were?

Oh yeah, because I worked as a bellhop in the—talking about the Rotender Line District? Oh yeah, they had quite a few bands out there. I couldn't recall the names of them because I wasn't paying too much ticket out, too busy working. I never could get a chance to go to them because I was working at night. See, I was a bellhop in a saloon.
Well, would they have the bands in the houses or the cribs or the cabarets or what?

No, they were in cabarets. Yeah, you had Pete Lawless at Rice Cafe, you had Tom Anderson. And Lula White, she just had a piano player. And Tom Anderson. And Pete Barrett, they didn't have no band. And there was about four or five places around there that had bands working. Well, Henry Martin, the drummer I was telling you about, he used to work with Peter Bocas. Peter Bocas. Was it Peter Bocas? I think it was Peter Bocas. I used to work with Peter Bocas at the Rice Cafe. And that's at the corner of Iberville and Murray. What was Pete playing?
Well, Cornet in them days, because Trumpet just come out around the late 30s, I believe.
